items.text: In this retrospective study, 220 patients with CF were analyzed using patient-level splitting to predict pulmonary exacerbations. The random forest model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.84. The model was not externally validated.

We included 165 patients with CF in a clinical decline classifier with patient-level splitting and nested cross-validation. The gradient-boosted model reached an AUC-ROC of 0.81. No external validation was performed.
This study evaluated 190 pwCF for hospital readmission risk using patient-level splitting. The neural survival model yielded AUCs of 0.78-0.83. The model was evaluated without independent validation.
We enrolled 260 patients with CF to forecast FEV1 trajectory under a patient-level split. Cross-validated regression reported an AUC-ROC of 0.79. The model was not tested on an independent cohort.

expected_grounding_substrings.external_validation: not tested on an independent cohort

items.text: A total of 310 patients with CF were included, and patient-level splitting prevented subject overlap across folds. Logistic regression achieved AUCs of 0.74-0.77. The classifier has never been externally validated.
We analyzed 240 patients with CF for acute exacerbation onset using a patient-level split. The classifier achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.83. The model will be externally validated using independent data.

We recruited 175 patients with CF and trained a prognostic pipeline with patient-level splitting. Cross-validation achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.80. An external validation cohort was identified for future evaluation.
In this retrospective analysis, 215 patients with CF were modeled with patient-level splitting. The ensemble reached AUCs of 0.76-0.81. There is no evidence that external validation was performed.

Methods included 290 patients with CF with patient-level splitting, and the abstract states the model was externally validated. Discussion notes an AUC-ROC of 0.85. Limitations state the model was not externally validated.
We evaluated 305 patients with CF using a patient-level split, obtaining an AUC-ROC of 0.82. In the report text, the model was externally validated, although no external validation was performed.

This was a single-center development study that included 420 patients with CF evaluated with a patient-level split. The model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.88. The model was externally validated on an independent cohort.

expected_grounding_substrings.external_validation: externally validated on an independent cohort

items.text: Across 14,200 sputum cultures from 185 pwCF, recurrent infection predictors were trained with patient-level splitting. Boosting achieved AUCs of 0.77-0.82. External validation is required before clinical use.

We studied 340 patients with CF alongside 12,000 longitudinal spirometry records using patient-level splitting. Mortality risk models achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.86. External validation was performed in an independent national registry.

Models trained on data from cells in HEK293T and 16HBE CFTR reporter assays screened 480 chemical analogs. The ridge model accurately predicted readthrough across PTC motifs. No patient cohort was enrolled.

Forskolin-induced swelling assays in 36 patient-derived rectal organoid lines trained an unsupervised clustering method for modulator stratification. Cluster analysis achieved dynamic quantification of CFTR function.

Airway mucociliary clearance abnormalities contribute to chronic neutrophilic inflammation in cystic fibrosis airways. Machine learning methods hold promise for characterizing longitudinal lung disease trajectories across heterogeneous cohorts.

We evaluated 230 patients with CF in a multi-year cohort using patient-level splitting to rank exacerbation risk. Survival gradient boosting reported a concordance index of 0.81 across folds. External validation was performed.
